tickets.name: Body assertions: assert.<path> on api nodes
tickets.description:
Problem: expect only checks the response STATUS. A flow that gets 200 back
with the wrong number in the body still scores green — FML confirms the API
responded, not that it said the right thing. Raised by a Claude session
working on stablishMind, testing an income calc (link bank -> sync ->
income): "the one thing to build first is body assertions ... without that,
FML tests are smoke tests not correctness tests." Confirmed against the
codebase 2026-10-09 — real gap, right priority call.

What to build: a new `assert.<name>: <expr>` dotted key on `api` nodes, same
shape as `capture.<var>` (repeatable, suffix is just a label for error
messages — not a variable name, nothing stores it). Reuses readPath() from
run.ts to pull the value out of the response, the same path syntax
capture already uses ($.data.income_rate, status, header.<Name>).

Comparison grammar for <expr>:
  - bare value           exact match after type coercion (assert.status: active)
  - ~N                   numeric, within tolerance of N (need to pick: relative
                          1% default, or require an explicit range like
                          ~11900+-50 -- decide before implementing, affects
                          the grammar)
  - >= <= > < !=          numeric comparison
  - anything else         treated as exact string match

Needs: readPath() currently can't resolve `.length` on an array (pathTokens
walks object keys / numeric indices only) -- `assert.sources.length: >= 2`
from the motivating example needs this. Add array .length as a special-cased
terminal token in readPath, not a general feature.

Failure semantics: match `expect`'s philosophy exactly -- an assert failure
marks the step failed (red) but does NOT stop the walk by itself; it follows
the drawn edge same as a failed status expect does today (stopOnFailure still
the fail-fast override). Captures run first, then expect, then asserts --
order matters because an assert can reference a value this same node just
captured.

Ripple (per CLAUDE.md -- language changes touch all of these):
  - src/fml/run.ts: buildRequest already reads node.data generically, this is
    new logic in runNode -- parse the comparison grammar, evaluate, fold into
    StepResult alongside captures/expect. readPath gets .length support.
  - src/fml/nodeTypes.ts: add "assert" to EXEC_KEY_PREFIXES so it's not
    flagged as an unknown key (same as header./query./capture.).
  - src/fml/lint.ts: malformed assert expression (bad operator, empty path)
    gets flagged the same way an empty capture.x: path is today.
  - HOW-TO.md: new section under the `api` keys reference, same treatment as
    the "Multiple hosts in one file" section.
  - examples/: extend one example (or add a new one) that fails on purpose
    via assert so the behavior is demonstrated, not just described.
  - Tests: run.test.ts (grammar parsing, .length on an array, pass/fail/stop
    semantics), lint.test.ts (malformed assert flagged).

Explicitly NOT in scope for this ticket (separate follow-ups, see
lore/ideas/flow-execution.md):
  - Conditional ROUTING on a captured/asserted value (branching on
    {income_rate} > 10000 instead of status) -- valuable but a different
    problem; this ticket is about scoring a step, not choosing an edge.
  - Test-data seeding / a `setup` node type -- FML has no backend-state
    concept today by design; probably stays Django's job (dedicated test
    fixtures/accounts) rather than something FML owns. Needs its own
    decision, not bundled in here.

Open question before starting: the tolerance syntax for ~N (relative %
default vs. requiring an explicit range) -- pick one before writing the
parser, it's the one part of the grammar without an obvious right answer.

tickets.name: Header assertion operators: matches (regex), exists, absent (extends FML-11)
tickets.description: DEPENDS ON FML-11. readPath already resolves header.<Name> (src/fml/run.ts), so assert.header.<Name> comes free with FML-11's assert grammar. This ticket only adds the operators FML-11 lacks: regex match, exists, absent. Motivation: Flock weak-ETag bug (W/"x") needed a regex/prefix check. See ideas/flock-audit-lore-fml.md.

tickets.name: Byte/hash assertions: sha256 of response body, content-length, 206/416 range checks
tickets.description: DEPENDS ON FML-11. Genuinely new: needs the runner to hold the raw response bytes (today only parsed text/JSON) so assert can compare sha256 and length, and a Range request header. Open design point: variable holding an expected hash. Decrypt-then-hash (Flock media) can be a separate follow-up; start with plain body sha256. Tests in run.test.ts.

tickets.name: Conditional GET example + docs: capture header.ETag then If-None-Match expects 304

Flock bug: edge rewrote ETag to weak and the origin's exact match returned 200.

tickets.name: Node sockets: visual variable wiring between nodes
tickets.description:
Raised by JB 2026-10-17, reference image attached (Blender/node-editor
sockets: typed in/out ports on a node, wired to another node's port).

Problem: a captured value is invisible plumbing today. capture.token on one
node creates {token}; a later node spends it by *typing* {token} into a
text field (auth, body, header.*, query.*, path). The data flow exists but
is never drawn -- you have to read two nodes' property panels side by side
to see it.

What to build: make the wiring visible and draggable, the way Blender's
sockets work.
  - Output ports: one per capture.<name> key a node has.
  - Input ports: one per distinct {name} the node references anywhere in
    its data (not per-field -- a name used in both header.X and body is one
    port, same variable).
  - Dragging a wire from an output port to an input port writes the same
    text a person would type by hand -- this is a new EDITOR interaction,
    not new engine behavior. src/fml/run.ts resolves {name} identically
    whichever way it got there. Write-back goes through src/lib/fmlEdit.ts
    the same as every other property-panel edit does today.

Open design questions -- decide before building, don't guess:
  1. Is a variable wire a second, visually distinct connection layer on the
     same canvas as the @flow arrows, or does it live somewhere else (a
     separate inspector view)? Leaning: second layer, same canvas,
     different color/style -- @flow edges are control flow (what runs
     next), variable wires are data flow (what value goes where). Blender
     keeps both on one graph; FML's @flow edges already ARE a graph on this
     canvas, so a second edge type reusing the same rendering machinery
     (src/components/edges/FlowEdge.tsx) is the natural fit -- but it needs
     its own visual language so the two are never confused at a glance.
  2. A field is free text, not a single typed slot -- `auth: bearer {token}`
     has a variable embedded in a literal string, not standing alone. Does
     a wire only connect to a field where the ENTIRE value is one {name}
     (simple, limited), or can dropping a wire onto a field insert {name}
     at the cursor / append it (matches how a person would actually type
     it, more useful, more edge cases: what if the field already has a
     different {name} in it, what does the wire visually anchor to then)?
  3. A node can reference the same {name} more than once in different
     fields (header.Authorization and a body field, say) -- does that
     collapse to one input port with multiple wires fanning in from the
     same source, or does connecting a wire from the port itself handle
     writing it into whichever field the person is looking at?

Non-goal: this does not change what @vars/capture mean or how run.ts
resolves them -- see src/fml/variables.ts and lore/ideas/flow-execution.md
for how that already works. Pure editor/canvas feature.

tickets.name: RML: RoadMap Language — sibling tool to FML for project roadmaps
tickets.description:
Raised by JB 2026-10-17, reference image attached (a game tech-tree: muted
vs. lit nodes, nodes with multiple incoming dependencies, grouped by
colour/category).

The idea: FML maps an API flow so you can see the logic executing. RML maps
a PROJECT so you can see where you are and what's next -- same visual
language (a typed, connected node graph), different subject. "lore and fml
are interlinked tools" -- RML is explicitly meant to be the third leg: a
roadmap node links out to the .fml file that proves it and the lore ticket
driving it.

What to build:
  - A new file type, .rml, structurally analogous to .fml: nodes + edges,
    but nodes are milestones/features and edges mean DEPENDS ON, not FLOWS
    TO. A node can depend on several others at once -- a DAG, not a tree
    (see reference image: nodes merge from multiple parents).
  - Architecture call, not forced, but worth starting from: FML's grammar
    (@meta / @nodes / @node <id> {} / arrows with -label>) is already
    generic enough to carry this -- it doesn't encode "flow" semantics
    anywhere in the parser itself, that meaning lives in nodeTypes.ts and
    in how run.ts walks edges. Reusing src/fml/parse.ts's block/edge
    grammar with a new node-type vocabulary (RML's equivalent of
    nodeTypes.ts) avoids re-implementing comment handling, line-oriented
    parsing, @fof-style includes, etc. a second time. Worth a real look
    before deciding to hand-roll a second parser.
  - A new top-center window/tab in the dashboard, alongside the existing
    doc list, to open and view .rml files -- same app, new view mode, not
    a separate deployed site.
  - Visual node state: muted (not done) vs. lit (done) at minimum --
    confirm with JB whether a third "in progress" state is wanted; the
    reference image reads as binary (locked/unlocked) but a roadmap
    arguably wants three.
  - Hover a node: title + one-line description (tooltip).
  - Click a node: opens a side panel (reuse the PropertyPanel pattern) with
    the full description, plus:
      - links to .fml files
      - links to lore tickets (FML-11-style ids)
    First cut can be a plain-text reference (just display "FML-11" / a
    file path as a label) rather than a live, resolved link -- see the
    dependency note below before promising more than that.

Dependency / open question: resolving a lore ticket link (showing the
ticket's actual name/status, not just its id) means reading
lore/workspace/ticket.json off disk from inside the browser app. That's
downstream of the "Open folder" / File System Access API item already
sitting in lore/CONTEXT.md's Open line -- RML shouldn't quietly reinvent
that. Decide: v1 ships with plain-text id labels and no live resolution, or
this waits on File System Access landing first.

Non-goal for v1: auto-deriving a node's muted/lit state from its linked
ticket's status. Useful eventually, but it's a second system (RML) reading
and trusting a third (ticket.json) automatically -- start with a human (or
agent) setting status: done/pending by hand on the rml node itself.

tickets.name: Create/delete nodes and edges from the dashboard
tickets.description:
Raised by JB 2026-10-17 as part of a larger ask ("create nodes in the web
dashboard"), split into its own ticket -- this part is concretely scoped;
see FML-23 for the live-sync half, which isn't.

Already flagged in lore/CONTEXT.md's Open line: "node rename + add/delete
node/edge (structural -- needs an FmlDoc->text serializer)". This ticket is
that item, written up properly.

Problem: every edit the dashboard can make today is targeted text surgery
on an EXISTING node/edge's span (src/lib/fmlEdit.ts -- "never re-serialises
the whole file", by design, so comments and formatting survive). There's no
operation for "this node doesn't exist in the text yet" -- you can't add a
node, delete a node, or add/delete an edge from the UI at all today.

What to build: the missing serializer half. Given an FmlDoc plus one
structural op (add node, delete node, add edge, delete edge), produce the
minimal text edit that does it -- same philosophy as fmlEdit.ts's existing
edits (surgical, not a full re-print of the doc), but these ops don't have
an existing span to anchor to, so this is new logic, not an extension of
the current targeted-replace functions.
  - Add node: insert an @nodes declaration line + an empty @node <id> {}
    block (or no block at all if the type has no expected keys -- a bare
    `Foo = page` is a complete, valid sketch, same as today's parser
    allows).
  - Delete node: remove its @nodes line, its @node {} block if present, and
    every @flow edge that touches it (orphaned edges are worse than a
    missing node).
  - Add/delete edge: a new/removed @flow line, including the grouped-edge
    syntax (multiple labelled arrows off one source) that already exists in
    the grammar.
  - Needs a place in the file to insert into -- decide where new content
    goes (end of @nodes / end of @flow, or some locality-preserving
    heuristic). Simplest correct answer: append; revisit only if JB finds
    it unreadable in practice.

This directly unblocks RML's "create nodes in the dashboard" requirement
too (FML-21) -- RML will want the same structural-edit capability for
.rml, so whatever shape this takes should be reusable, not FML-specific
where it doesn't have to be.

Non-goal: this ticket is about the file edit, not UI chrome (an "add node"
button, a node-type picker, etc.) -- those are straightforward once the
serializer exists and don't need their own ticket.

tickets.name: Live agent<->dashboard sync, no manual save (design-first)
tickets.description:
Raised by JB 2026-10-17 as part of a larger ask, split from FML-22 (adding
nodes in the dashboard) because this half is a different shape of problem --
open-ended, not yet scoped to an implementation. JB's own words: "if
dashboard isn't the right tool for this am willing to look for other
options too" -- treat that as real, not a formality. Design this before
building it.

The ask: when an agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) edits a .fml/.rml file on
disk directly, the open dashboard reflects the change live -- no save
button, no manual reload. And the reverse direction (JB edits the canvas,
the agent sees it without JB saving) is implied too -- "like cowork".

Why this doesn't have a cheap answer:
  - A static site has nothing to watch a file with. The browser's only
    primitive is File System Access (showDirectoryPicker + a handle), which
    gets you read access but no push-based change events -- you'd have to
    poll getFile() on an interval, which is laggy and burns cycles for
    something that wants to feel instant.
  - A real live-watch wants a small local process (chokidar / fs.watch)
    pushing change events over a socket to the page -- same shape as
    vite/devProxy.ts (apply: "serve", dev-only, never ships to
    protoarch.web.app). Meaning: this feature, however it's built, almost
    certainly only works while running the dev server locally, not on the
    deployed site. Confirm that's an acceptable shape before building
    toward it.
  - The two-way version is the actually hard part: if JB is mid-drag on the
    canvas the instant an agent writes the file, something has to decide
    what wins. That's the same class of problem as Figma/Google Docs
    collaborative editing between two live editors -- it does not have an
    obvious cheap answer, and guessing at one before it's designed is how
    you end up silently eating someone's edit.

Recommended first cut, to get something real without solving the hard
problem: ONE-WAY sync only -- agent/file changes push into the dashboard
live (read-only reflect), JB's own edits still go through the existing
save/write-back path (FML-22). This sidesteps the conflict question
entirely for v1 and is still a large, real capability (JB watches an agent
work, without refreshing). Two-way "cowork" stays a v2 decision, made once
the one-way version has been lived with.

Non-goal for this ticket: implementing anything. This is a design pass --
leaves with a decided architecture (confirm/replace the local-watcher-only
assumption above) and a scoped v1 (one-way reflect), handed off as a new,
concretely-scoped ticket once that's settled.
